# Independent performance review — runtime-evidence addendum

Verdict: **PASS for this task's source-bound static review and small-fixture runtime evidence**. No unresolved blocking performance finding. This verdict does not certify IDE startup, large-project performance, a memory budget, hardware responsiveness, full-app integration or completion of Phase1/the IDE.

Source commit: 830ff53de76dbecd5fc3761f1c5f5bae164763c2 in /workspace/android-studio-source-providers. Production SHA-256 generated_artifacts.rs 5264e4c00d8958a4aaee250c7d924ae89e4665f778b893156442f6af3ed52be0; bridge SHA 508ecc9987932f8d184983f551eca0cb1bc9efa6ed12806dcaff8a0a2f6880b7; tests SHA 9900069b1a993875795c4be1feadf5f4a8da2a5750f486beb4596ae6b45efbf1. These are the reviewed final sources; no production performance algorithm changed after the earlier static pass.

## Independent verification performed

I read the raw logs, command/result records, compiler JSON artifacts, current probe source, inspection/model outputs, source guards, toolchain proof and final cleanup record. All 8 frozen source/data hashes, 184 immutable originals and all 4,612 fixed-scope whole-source hashes matched current bytes. The 13 original private-fixture input hashes matched both the original fixture and restored private copy. All 10 toolchain proof files matched their byte counts and hashes. This review did not run Cargo, Gradle, the probe or the app.

The compiler artifacts identify this worktree's package/source paths and fresh=false for the newly compiled library, unit-test ELF and 28-test generated_artifacts ELF. The crate-root freshness receipt preserves identical bytes before/after its mtime touch. The exact normal-Cargo library linked into the runtime probe currently matches SHA bf2d8ee866f659ee864387a311a0749c168b3c2e6fb06c06226ca8f0713e00ff. Probe source SHA 5551985487b7e87f31963365ccf203f138de5f7bb4ebb2d5f4ca9d9b9a971dca and probe ELF SHA 531cc5f5ee7ca35a304513a9f8ab0b8f7246232e8674a10fa5239f4dfd19702f also matched, as did the retained unit-test and generated-artifact test ELFs. The frozen runtime bridge is byte-exact to production.

The unfiltered normal Cargo log contains 202 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored, 0 filtered tests across six suites (85+28+20+21+29+19). Strict ./script/clippy expands to release/all-targets/all-features/deny-warnings and exits0; formatting and normal library build also exit0. Compiler-inclusive test peak 1,802,572 KiB and Clippy aggregate peak 1,076,280 KiB are build-tool observations, not IDE runtime budgets. A retained failed initial launch was not promoted into a successful gate.

## Small-fixture runtime observations

The fresh official SDK executions use AGP9.4.0, model producer23.0/minimum consumer66.1, Gradle9.6.1, JDK21.0.12.1+1, platform37/build-tools37.0.0. Toolchain records explicitly mark this supplementary rather than pinned Studio runtime equivalence. Each captured model contains one Android module and two variants. Each Gradle log contains exactly one model record and BUILD SUCCESSFUL; each matching Rust assertion process exits0 with empty stderr. These are actual current probes, not the old planning probes.

| Mode | Model record bytes | Rust probe process ms | Rust probe peak KiB | Gradle invocation seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| source | 68135 | 5.134 | 10496 | 14.759 |
| bytecode | 68498 | 5.082 | 10496 | 10.578 |
| custom | 68135 | 5.349 | 10496 | 11.635 |
| disabled | 67255 | 5.609 | 10496 | 11.278 |
| disabled-artifact | 68135 | 7.990 | 10496 | 11.065 |

The Rust figures above measure the **entire isolated validation process**, including launch, file I/O, Basic model decoding, sidecar decoding, revision/feature/artifact checks, fixture-output assertions and JSON serialization. The inspected runtime-probe.rs performs all these operations. The field name decoderProcessPeakRssKiB in the raw receipt must not be read as decoder-only memory; neither isolated decoder latency nor incremental Rust heap cost was measured. The boundary assertion process similarly reports 1.777ms/9,216KiB for the entire process and verifies all11 synthetic getter boundary cases; it is not official SDK getter timing.

The five Gradle invocation elapsed times include configuration, selected producer/inspection tasks, model construction and serialization. They are not per-getter timings. Their launcher-process peak records (536,536–646,480KiB) explicitly exclude the separately running Gradle daemon's RSS, so they cannot establish whole-build JVM memory. Runs are one observation per mode in a shared prepared fixture/cache; they are not controlled cold/warm comparisons or statistical performance distributions.

The runtime-measurement-method.json provenance addendum reports os.posix_spawn followed by per-PID os.wait4/Linux ru_maxrss. I verified its twelve command/PID/elapsed triples exactly match the original receipts. **The exact executed measurement runner source was not retained**, and the addendum candidly says so; I cannot independently inspect that executed launch/measurement implementation. Therefore this review accepts the figures only as reported per-process observations tied to current execution receipts and artifacts. It does not treat them as a reproducible benchmark, absolute ceiling or proof of a specified implementation's allocator use. The original twelve receipts remain preserved.

## Static assessment retained

Module validation still checks exact ordered identities then zips them in O(M), rather than performing the former O(M²) per-module search. GeneratedRecord still ignores unrelated Basic fields and moves only the sidecar Value into its DTO. ObjectOnly imposes constant root-shape dispatch per wire object, without new full-model copies or repeated full-model traversals. The 16 MiB record limit still precedes JSON materialization. Collection uniqueness costs remain O(N log N), raw path encounter order and duplicates remain retained, and there is no new filesystem scan/UI callback/startup hook. The 600,000-character unrelated field and strict positional-shape cases now belong to the actually passing28-test suite, but they do not constitute large-project timing or RSS proof.

Advisory duplicate Versions/BasicAndroidProject SDK queries, JVM canonicalPath cost and potential repeated same-revision identity cloning remain unchanged. The current small fixture supplies no evidence that justifies a new blocker or an estimate for thousands of modules. The 16 MiB limit is a wire-input decoding limit, not a total-process or JVM memory ceiling.

## Cleanup and remaining integration scope

All five owned Gradle daemon log hashes match the final receipt and show shutdown; their PIDs254416/254518/254619/254759/254860 are currently absent. The cleanup record reports launcher/probe closure, fixture restoration, whole-source/index-content preservation and no unowned process termination. The unrelated daemon167092 was left untouched. Index byte changes after refresh are explicitly explained as stat/cache metadata; clean content and whole-source hashes remained preserved.

This task still requires the lead's combined app/native/full-CI/parity-capture gates before integration. No five generated-tree reference-flow credit follows from these small SDK probes, and no total reference-census completion is claimed. Full-app startup, responsiveness, hardware GPU behavior and large-project runtime remain outside this addendum.

No runtime/compiler/SDK/app command, cache mutation, product edit, test weakening or subagent spawn was performed by this reviewer. Earlier PASS/FAIL reports are retained. Suggested .rules additions: none.
